input.description: Search for email handling and route wiring

input.reason: I read src/jira.ts and its only caller in src/routes.ts. At src/jira.ts:9, `email` goes straight into a double-quoted JQL literal: `assignee = "${email}" ORDER BY created DESC`. The encodeURIComponent call at line 10 only encodes the finished JQL for the URL. It does not escape JQL string syntax, so the Jira server still receives a raw `"` after decoding. The only caller, routes.ts:56 (`searchAssigned(req.body.email)`), passes the request body field with no validation, and nothing else in src checks or sanitizes email. A `"` in the value therefore ends the literal and lets the caller append their own JQL clauses.
input.summary: searchAssigned interpolates unescaped email into JQL query

findings.text: `searchAssigned` puts `email` into the JQL string without escaping. A value containing `"` rewrites the query. Escape `\` and `"` before interpolating.
findings.reason: Claim 1, that email goes into the JQL string without escaping: src/jira.ts:9 builds `assignee = "${email}" ORDER BY created DESC` from the raw parameter. The encodeURIComponent at line 10 is applied to the whole JQL string for the URL only, and Jira decodes it back to the unescaped JQL. Claim 2, that a value containing `"` rewrites the query: the value sits inside a double-quoted JQL literal, so a `"` closes it and whatever follows is read as JQL (for example `x" OR project = FOO OR assignee = "y`). The input is attacker-controlled: routes.ts:56 passes `req.body.email` directly, and nothing in src validates or escapes it. The suggested fix is left as written.

evidence.code: const jql = `assignee = "${email}" ORDER BY created DESC`;

input.severity_reason: This is a real JQL injection from request input (routes.ts:56 → jira.ts:9), so callers can run arbitrary Jira searches. The impact is limited. The fetch at jira.ts:10 sends no credentials, so injected queries run with the same Jira access as normal queries. Callers can also already query any assignee, because email is not tied to req.user. The injection lets them build arbitrary queries rather than gain new privileges, which makes it a significant risk but not a critical one.
